note.explanation: Responsible internet use means staying safe, checking information, protecting privacy, treating others respectfully, and balancing online time with offline life.
examples: Before trusting a health claim online, compare it with information from several trustworthy websites.
If someone sends you a suspicious link, do not click it; use the platform’s report or block tools if needed.
note.checkAnswer: Check several trustworthy sources and avoid sharing personal information on unfamiliar websites.
note.simple: Use the internet carefully: check what you read, protect your personal information, be kind to people, and take breaks.
note.checkQuestion: Name one way to check online information and one way to protect your privacy during research.
note.title: Responsible Internet Use
steps: Check important information against several trustworthy sources.
Avoid sensational headlines and suspicious links.
Use private browsing and do not enter personal information on unfamiliar websites.
Set time limits, take breaks, and include offline activities.
Set social media privacy controls and interact respectfully.
Report and block cyberbullying, and support the person being bullied.
note.answer: Use the internet safely and respectfully, protect your privacy, check information, and maintain a healthy balance between online and offline activities.

written.text: Discuss the concept of internet addiction and its potential impact on individuals. How can recognizing the signs of addiction, setting time limits, and finding offline activities help promote balanced internet usage?
written.finalAnswer: Internet addiction is spending so much time online that it interferes with daily life; recognising its signs, setting time limits, and balancing online use with offline activities can help promote healthy internet use.

rubric.why: This gives the section’s definition of internet addiction.
rubric.how: Explain that excessive time online interferes with daily life.

rubric.why: Recognising signs helps a person notice unhealthy internet use.
rubric.how: Mention difficulty stopping or neglecting sleep, study, or relationships.

rubric.description: Give the balancing strategy and final answer.
rubric.how: Mention activities such as sports, reading, or meeting friends in person and summarise the balanced-use idea.

modelAnswer: Internet addiction happens when a person spends so much time online that it starts to interfere with their daily life.
A sign is finding it hard to stop using the internet when it is time to sleep, study, or spend time with family and friends.
Setting time limits and sticking to them can help prevent internet addiction.
Offline activities such as sports, reading, or spending time with friends in person help balance online time.

Final answer: Internet addiction is spending so much time online that it interferes with daily life; recognising its signs, setting time limits, and balancing online use with offline activities can help promote healthy internet use.

explain.title: Check information before trusting it
explain.body: Do not rely on only one website. Compare information with other trustworthy sources. Be skeptical of sensational or misleading headlines, because they may be used to spread false information.

explain.title: Protect your privacy while researching
explain.body: Private or incognito browsing does not save browsing history or personal information in the usual way. Avoid entering personal information on unfamiliar websites and do not click links that seem strange or too good to be true.

explain.title: Balance online time
explain.body: Internet addiction happens when a person spends so much time online that it starts to interfere with their daily life. Set time limits, take breaks, use time-management features, and make room for offline activities.

explain.title: Be safe and respectful on social networks
explain.body: Adjust privacy settings so only trusted people can see your posts. Use polite language and do not spread rumours or false information. If you see cyberbullying, report and block the person responsible and support the person affected.

mistakes: Trusting a claim because it appears on one website instead of cross-checking it.
Assuming a sensational headline is reliable without checking the information.
Entering personal details on unfamiliar websites or clicking suspicious links.
Thinking private browsing makes every website safe or hides all activity from everyone.
Ignoring sleep, study, or relationships while spending too much time online.
Replying to cyberbullying with insults or sharing the harmful post further.
